align.prompt: LLM ablation baseline for eu-gbr-london, variant orig-llm-skeleton2grid-opus5: maximise H/V.

transcript.note: Round 1, criterion 1 (take H/V wherever reachable in 1-3 cells) plus criterion 4 (never touch the shared coordinate of an already-aligned chain). I first built the lock table from hvSegs: 34 of 103 points are locked on both axes and were excluded outright; every move below only touches an axis that carries no H/V segment. (a) Free leaves, one segment each, no winding risk: 21 -> col 58 (V into 48), 42 -> col 38 (V into 29), 56 -> col 3 (V into 92). (b) Paired move to close a long diagonal: 38 and 39 both to col 19 (39's row 58 is untouched so its H into 33 survives). (c) Best value per move, 68 -> (56,49): it joins the col-56 trunk 73/100/7 and closes TWO segments at once (68-7 and 68-64 both become V), and drops 43-68 onto an exact 45 as a by-product. (d) Single-axis slides onto a neighbour's locked coordinate: 28 -> row 55 (H into 29, chosen over moving 29 because moving 29 would have destroyed the 29-30 45), 89 -> row 48 (H into 97), 32 -> row 47 (H into 52, upgrading that 45 to H; col 38 was the tempting alternative but 32 would then sit ON the 102-52 vertical and be swallowed), 79 -> col 38 (V into 53), 19 -> col 48 (V into 18; this also drops 19-71 to 45. I deliberately did NOT also pull 71 onto row 31 - it would land inside the 19-31 horizontal and be swallowed), 27 -> row 33 (H into 99), 40 -> row 47 (H into 37), 86 -> row 41 (H into 75, upgrading that 45). (e) 49 -> (62,37) was the one real trade: it gives up the 45-49 45 but buys 49-0 as H and drops 49-70 to 45, so H/V is up and the 45 count is unchanged. Row 37 was chosen over row 40 for exactly that reason. (f) Two consolation 45s where H/V is out of range: 50 -> col 31 (45 into 52) and 95 -> col 51 (a staging step; next round it goes to col 50 to become V with 77 and 45 with 80 in one shot - 54->50 is 4 cells, over the short-move limit, so it has to be split). Rejected after checking edge winding: 5 -> row 37 (would have bought two H, but it swings 5 from north-east of 24 to due east, crossing 23's bearing and reversing the order at 24) and 24/23 -> col 52 (same crossing at 24).
